fullText:
DUBAI/WASHINGTON, Sept 20 (Reuters) - Iran and the United States exchanged new threats on Sunday, with President Donald Trump warning Iran would fail economically or face its leadership being wiped out if it didn't make a deal, and the Iranian ‌military saying it would retaliate harshly to any fresh attack.

The conflict has looked stalemated for months, with no sign either side was ready ‌for concessions even as it has deepened a global energy crisis, cratered swathes of Iran's economy and spilled over into new regional escalations.

In a phone call with a Fox News reporter, Trump ​said Iran's leaders should make a deal, rot economically or be wiped out, the reporter said.

However, with Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian expected in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly, Trump said he would be open to meeting him, the Fox reporter added.

Trump has repeatedly made vague threats of major military escalations during the conflict that began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28, without carrying them out.

Earlier, Iran's military central command said any new attack would trigger sustained ‌retaliation against US bases and interests and that Washington's ⁠regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict.

The Iranian military added that it had information that an attack was being prepared, without elaborating on what that information might be.

US Gulf allies have already been badly scarred by a ⁠war that the US and Israel launched with no warning, bringing their cities under Iranian fire and hammering their economies with the crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway blockaded.

On Saturday their predicament worsened further, with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi group launching missile and drone strikes at the Saudi capital after having made sudden military gains in Yemen's reignited civil war ​earlier ​this month.

The US State Department ‌issued a security alert citing the Houthi hostilities. It said there was potential for unforeseen escalation in the Middle East, and Americans should exercise more vigilance and be aware of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.

Saudi Arabia did not comment on the incident, though a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had foiled other attacks on the kingdom.

Recent escalation by the Houthis has forced Riyadh into a painful dilemma: continue airstrikes on the group to stop it seizing more Yemeni territory or step back in the hopes of averting drone strikes on critical infrastructure.

The Houthi gains along the coast mean the group's forces ‌now sit on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, giving them easier control over shipping travelling between ​the Red Sea and Asia and the ability to blockade the crucial waterway.

With Iran already ​having blockaded most shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the oil-rich Gulf's ​energy exports are now almost entirely cut off from global markets, adding to pressure on oil prices.

A US blockade of ‌Iranian ports is meanwhile stopping Iran from selling its own oil, ​contributing to major problems in the Islamic ​Republic's economy.

Despite the economic damage, there is little sign of a return to the interim ceasefire agreement that was struck in June but fell apart in July amid disputes over its terms.

Iran reiterated on Sunday that it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the terms ​of that June agreement, as it interpreted them, were met.

Iranian ‌Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran would have to keep on fighting as well as negotiating, to push back its enemies ​and to consolidate any gains with diplomacy.

title: What have we learned from the Premier League so far?
description: BBC Sport takes a look at the opening weeks of the Premier League season as a long international break arrives.
fullText:
The Premier League takes a near three-week break as we enter a four-game international window.

So, what have we learned from the opening five matches of the season?

Premier League champions Arsenal were looking fairly unstoppable in the opening weeks of the season.

A win over Brighton on Saturday would have given the Gunners a club-record equalling eighth consecutive win in all competitions to start the season.

But that all ended with a 3-0 loss at Amex Stadium on Saturday.

The Gunners had not lost a league game by more than one goal, let alone three, since October 2024.

It was their heaviest defeat in the league since May 2023 when they lost 3-0 to the same opposition.

"That's not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup," said boss Mikel Arteta.

"What we've done, the way we've competed and the amount of games we've won has been remarkable - but this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level."

Brighton humbling 'a big lesson' for Arsenal - Arteta

Many wondered if Manchester City would experience a post-Pep Guardiola slump when the legendary boss left after a decade.

Things did not start too well under Enzo Maresca, with the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal.

But they have won all five games in the Premier League - and seven in a row in all competitions - after Sunday's entertaining 5-3 win over Sunderland.

That takes them three points clear of Arsenal.

"In the press conference before the game, I said I expect a very tough game," said Maresca. "Then we also conceded two or three goals but we have learned a lot in these eight weeks and this is good."

Perfect 24 hours as Man City put pressure on Arsenal

Brighton and Brentford, two clubs who have never won a major trophy, have continued to impress this season.

Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton enjoyed that 3-0 win over Arsenal to see them sit third in the table, only two points behind the Gunners.

Brighton have won at home against the reigning Premier League champions in each of the last three seasons.

Star player Pascal Gross laughed and said "no" when BBC Sport asked him if Albion were in the title race.

But stranger things have happened...

Meanwhile, just one point below them in the table are Keith Andrews' Brentford.

Many tipped the Bees to struggle after the departure of Thomas Frank last summer but if anything they improved under their former set-piece coach Andrews.

And their start to this season - unbeaten after five games and fourth in the table - is showing he is no one-season wonder as a manager.

They go into the break on the back of their most impressive result, a 3-0 home win over Chelsea.

Leeds, impressing again under boss Daniel Farke, are also on nine points and in a potential Champions League place.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool and Everton are just below them on goal difference.

From near oblivion to Europe - Brighton celebrate 125th anniversary in style

Seven years apart, United did the same thing twice hoping for different results - appointing a club legend who last managed in Britain in the Championship after a good start as caretaker boss.

In 2019 it was Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and this time it was Michael Carrick.

But this season, after Carrick having a summer to work on his team, the Red Devils have only won once in the league.

Their five points after five league games is their joint fewest at this stage of a Premier League season.

They go into the international break on the back of a 1-1 draw against Fulham, and even needed a late deflected Matheus Cunha strike to stop the Cottagers winning their first game all season.

After the Lisandro Martinez own goal that give Fulham the lead, ex-United captain Gary Neville said on Sky Sports: "I've watched Manchester United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen.

"Absolutely pathetic. I've never seen such a lack of effort."

United's owners will have almost three weeks to stew on this before they host fellow underachievers Tottenham (more on them soon) on 10 October.

In 2024 and 2025, the three promoted teams went straight back down - mostly with really low points tallies too.

But that streak came to an end last year when Sunderland finished seventh to qualify for Europe and Leeds came 14th. Only Burnley went down.

And the early weeks of this season indicate we could be in for a similar situation.

Hull City are eighth after five games, with their 2-1 loss to Newcastle their first defeat.

Ipswich are 11th. And Coventry, after losing the first four games without scoring, beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 and only sit in the drop zone on goal difference.

A Coventry win 25 years in the making

Tottenham finished 17th the last two seasons, their lowest two finishes since being in the second tier in 1977-78.

But expectations were raised after a summer of big spending - with Spurs splashing out £302m as well as making two high-profile loan signings.

Defence and midfield in particular were overhauled, with new wingers too.

But they are left with one senior striker in Dominic Solanke, who has only scored 12 Premier League goals in over two years at the club.

"I feel they have overpaid for every player they bought this summer - you can't rule them out from being in and around the relegation battle," said TNT pundit and ex-England international Joe Cole.

Saturday's 3-2 loss against Aston Villa sees them sit 19th going into the break - despite scoring their first two league goals of the campaign.

"We have to put on the pitch something more than we are putting," said manager Roberto de Zerbi.

"Football is tactical but it is blood, it is fighting, it is first one on the ball. We will suffer until the next game."

No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat

Many were keen to see what Xabi Alonso could do at Chelsea this season.

The Spaniard memorably led Bayer Leverkusen to a historic unbeaten German double in 2023-24.

And they made big changes to their squad this summer, with £117m attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers and new first-choice keeper Emiliano Martinez both coming in from Aston Villa.

There have been 22 goals in their five league games - more coming against them than for them - and they sit 10th.

And that is not even counting the 6-3 win over Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

Hugely entertaining for the neutrals - but perhaps not for Chelsea fans or management.

title: Liverpool have signed one of the best in the world, he's incredible
description: Liverpool have an incredible player who could win the Ballon d'Or very soon. In the history of the Reds, there's only been one Ballon d'Or winner. There should have been more. Mo Salah and Virgil van ...
fullText:
Liverpool have an incredible player who could win the Ballon d'Or very soon.

In the history of the Reds, there's only been one Ballon d'Or winner. There should have been more. Mo Salah and Virgil van Dijk have definitely made a case for it in the past.

But they existed in a world where Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo were superhuman. They were impossible to stop from winning those Ballon d'Ors, they were simply in a league of their own.

So, that means Liverpool's only Ballon d'Or winner to date is Michael Owen. Yes, Michael Owen. Not Steven Gerrard, not Kenny Dalglish or Ian Rush but Owen.

A player whose legacy at Anfield is very much tarnished by the way he left for Real Madrid and then joined Manchester United.

The era of Ronaldo and Messi is coming to an end now though. Both of them are fizzling out of the elite level and there's a new generation looking to win their fair share of the accolades.

Kylian Mbappe is probably at the forefront. He will be one of the favourites to win the award this year. Harry Kane will be another.

After Rodri and Ousmane Dembele having won the award, the Ballon d'Or is certainly a lot more attainable for anyone.

Liverpool have an exciting new generation who will be motivated to play a role and leave their legacy on the modern game.

Among those players will be the likes of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola. But there's another who if he keeps going will win the Ballon d'Or.

In the history of the award, there haven't been many centre-backs to have won the accolade.

It's an achievement reserved for the very best. Fabio Cannavaro won it after Italy won the World Cup. And while Rodri wasn't a centre-back, winning the award as a holding midfielder after Spain won the Euros is also a notable achievement.

The key denominator here is that first and foremost you have to be one of the best in the world, and you have to experience tournament success.

Jacquet already ticks one of those boxes. Based on his form, the Reds have signed one of the best defenders on the planet.

The fact that he plays for France, who are likely to be successful at the Euros and the World Cups in the future means if he keeps going the way he is, he will win a Ballon d'Or, it's simply inevitable.

title: Juventus 2 – Atalanta 0: Initial reaction and random observations
description: Juventus went into the first international break of the season with their second win in the span of four days, beating the always-tricky Atalanta in the process.
fullText:
Following last Sunday's last-second loss to Sassuolo, Juventus had 180 minutes to try and get back on track a little bit before the first international break of the season arrived. It involved two very different kinds of opponents — a struggling Dutch side and a domestic opponent that Juve had barely had any success against at the Allianz Stadium over the past decade.

Thursday night saw the first Europa League fixture passed with flying colors, the kind of one-sided scoreline on the scoreboard in Europe that we haven't seen from Juventus much at all in the past few decades.

And what about Sunday's return to Serie A?

Well, it wasn't a 5-0 win like against NEC Nijmegen, but it was a return to winning ways domestically.

Thanks to a second half in which Atalanta rarely looked all that dangerous, Juventus were able to put La Dea away with a towering Gleison Bremer header and claim a 2-0 victory at the Allianz Stadium. It marked Juventus' first home victory over Atalanta since the pre-COVID days of 2018 — something that both speaks to how the Boys from Bergamo had previously risen to be a constant thorn in the Bianconeri's side but also how the current state of the club is far from where it was seven or eight years ago.

We can say the same about Juventus, of course. See what we saw last weekend against Sassuolo is reminder of just how far off the 2018 version they currently are.

But on this day, with the opposing manager being the last man to lift the Scudetto in Turin, Juventus looked much, much better than the team they lined up against.

There was no stretched defense for much of the second half. There was no worrying when the hammer would fall because Juventus' game state was just all over the damn place. As compared to seven days earlier, how Luciano Spalletti's squad closed out the game was a breath of fresh and the hope is that it continues once this lengthy international break actually comes to a close during the second weekend of October. (Yes, it's that long of a break.)

Things weren't great for Juventus in the first half. That's even after Francisco Conceição gave them the lead in the 28th minute. Juve recorded all of three shots total against the team that entered Sunday's game allowing the most shots per game in Serie A so far this season. Things looked OK, but nothing to be overly excited about.

The second half, though, that was a change for the better. A much-needed change for the better to see out the win, too.

Was it the change at the half to bring on Pape Matar Sarr and have a little more steel and running in the midfield? Was it the fact that it looked like Maurizio Sarri didn't change much of anything at the half? Or maybe it was just simply Juventus playing better than they did in the opening 45 minutes?

Either way, Juve really did control the second half in a way that we couldn't say about the way things went to begin the game.

You combine this with the win over NEC midweek and it's the kind of response you were hoping to see from Juventus following the loss to Sassuolo. That doesn't mean that everything is all good now and there's no reason to worry anymore. There's still a host of injuries to important players, with many of them being long-term absences. There are much tougher opponents on the schedule before the second international break of the season arrives and those same players are back from injury.

But when you consider the immediate future, Spalletti and Juventus did well to get through the first steps of the difficult moment. They got two wins when they needed to and now go into the break with a little less heat on them as compared to where things stood seven days earlier.

Thankfully that's the case because seeing Juventus lose a second straight Serie A fixture would have been brutal for a club that is already dealing with long-term injuries up and down the roster with no immediate respite in sight. Now we just hope that Juventus players don't go out and then come back from international duty with the same kinds of injuries we've seen from previous international breaks.

It sure was nice to hear Allianz Stadium singing in the way they were at the end of that game. Feels like it's been a while since we've heard that strong of a voice from the supporters. (Not like they've had a ton to be happy about the last couple of years, but we know they are a driving force in a lot of ways.)

Ah, yes … Mauruzio Sarri going with an Atalanta midfield three of players who have all been linked with moves to Juventus within the last couple of years. Instead, they all ended up in Bergamo.

This Atalanta … not like the Atalanta of a couple of years ago, folks.

Is that because they no longer have Teun Koopmeiners? (Don't answer that. Let the joke sit.)

In all seriousness, though, Koopmeiners was perfectly OK as Juve saw the win out. He did his job.

More importantly, another signing by Cristiano Giuntoli — you know, the guy who is now in charge of building Atalanta's roster — continues to look pretty good for Juventus. That would be Douglas Luiz. That decision by Spalletti to keep him around this summer is looking better and better by the week.

And we're getting Douglas Luiz sombreros in the closing minutes of a Juve win now? My goodness.

Dad was at the stadium! Everybody look at how good Dad looks!

That man is a couple of months away from being 52 years old and looks fantastic. It's not just because of the beard that he continues to roll (incredibly well), either.

How many different positions did Weston McKennie play in this game? Because I lost track. I seriously did.

Sure like when Bremer plays like this as compared to whatever it was he was doing against Sassuolo. This Bremer is a lot better than that version. And the proof was in just how strong Juve were defensively on top of his scoring the goal that put Atalanta away.

While Randal Kolo Muani didn't score a goal on Sunday, this sure felt like the kind of game we could get used to seeing from him. Should he have scored? Yeah, maybe. But it was everything else that he did that was an encouraging sign that he may be starting to seriously get out of his struggles from the first couple of weeks of the season. My man was active — and a lot of the good things Juve did in attack went through him. More of this, Randal, because the goals will follow it this kind of performance becomes a regular thing.

Seriously, some of the one-touch passing sequences that Kolo Muani was involved in were just lovely.

Thankfully Juventus were up 2-0 in the final minutes because the visual of Nick Woltemade basically running toward three or four Atalanta defenders on the counter with nobody else in bianconero around him was amusing. It's different if it's a 0-0 game, of course.

Woltemade is just German for giraffe. At least that's what I think it means.

Guglielmo Vicario had to make one save in this game. It was a good one.

But that doesn't mean Vicario was just a total spectator against Atalanta. He had plenty of his patrolling of his penalty area to do. And he did it well — which pretty much had me thinking about how Juve's last starting goalkeeper probably wouldn't have done it as well as Vic did. For that, I am thankful.

Starting to really like what Pape Sarr brings to Juventus' midfield. More of that after the international break.

Zeki Celik good. And now we're getting assists? Not bad for a guy who hasn't played much on the left.

You know who is also good? Jhon Lucumí. That man defended his ass off against Atalanta.

I would like if the version of Pierre Kalulu from last season showed up again. He has not been that good in both phases of the game so far this season. His crossing has been off. Same can be said for his defending. And let's just not discuss the risk he ran with the pulling of a player's jersey in the box from the first half. A different day and a different referee and that could have been a PK at a point where Juve didn't need it.

This is a classic Conceição kind of game, right? As much as the goal is the highlight for him, there's also so many questionable decisions that he made that leaves you just wanting more.

Edon Zhegrova with an assist after his two-goal game against Sassuolo last weekend. Not bad.

This Sunday was better than last Sunday. I feel like that is not a very controversial opinion.

That's also a pretty good way to go into an international break — especially one where the Italian papers are going to totally over-discuss certain talking points because of the extra week thrown in there despite how many games Gli Azzurri play.

So yes, we crack open the bourbon for good times this weekend. Certainly not for the reasons of last weekend. For that, I am also very thankful.

title: Pulisic ends Milan goal drought days after missing out on USMNT camp 🇺🇸
description: Just days after missing out on Mauricio Pochettino's latest USMNT squad for the upcoming extended international break, Christian Pulisic is back among the goals as Milan lock horns with Lecce at San S...
fullText:
Just days after missing out on Mauricio Pochettino's latest USMNT squad for the upcoming extended international break, Christian Pulisic is back among the goals as Milan lock horns with Lecce at San Siro.

It's been a different period for the American star of late, but hope seemingly arrived in the vein of Ruben Amorim this summer, who viewed Pulisic as 'perfect for the way I think (about) football.'

But fast-forward to the present, where the 28-year-old has routinely been left out by the Portuguese tactician, Pulisic was handed a start as the Rossoneri looked to continue their undefeated start to the 2026/27 Serie A season.

He delivered when called upon in the opening half to break the deadlock against Salentini, doing well to bring down Strahinja Pavlović's ball over the top before gliding home past Wladimiro Falcone.

It was the first time Pulisic found the back of the net in his last 39 shots in Serie A, putting an end to an embarrassing barren run in front of goal.

A first goal since December 2025 and on his first start of the season is certainly one way to, hopefully, begin to silence some of his critics as the key attacker looks to get back to his best.
